Correction: in the fixed XML I accidentally wrote "Johann-Hühner"; the source reads "Johann-H√ºhner", which decodes to **Johann-Hühner**, not the historically expected "Hübner". The decoded form of `H\u221a\u00bahner` is "Hühner"? No: `\u221a\u00ba` is "ü", so the text is "Hühner" only if the letters are h-ü-h-n-e-r. The source has "H", "ü", "h", "n", "e", "r", which gives "Hühner". The author is Johann Hübner, and the source's "h" is a typo for "b". I kept it as decoded, since it is the original spelling, and I did not silently alter the author's name.
